admire.simple: to respect and like someone greatly
admire.natural: He admired the officer's calm manner at the gate.
admire.positive: We admire people who stay kind when they have power.
admire.leadership: A leader earns admiration by doing the hard work himself first.
admire.factual: The unit admired the cadet who completed the march with a sprained ankle.
admire.general: I admire the way she handles difficult customers.

concern.natural: Her concern showed in the questions she asked.
concern.positive: Showing concern early prevents small problems from growing.
concern.leadership: A leader listens to a junior's concern before giving orders.
concern.factual: Safety is the main concern during night training.
concern.general: He raised a concern about the seating arrangement.

decide.natural: He decided quickly and then stood by it.
decide.positive: Deciding on time is better than deciding perfectly late.
decide.leadership: A leader decides with the facts he has, then takes responsibility.
decide.factual: The committee decided to postpone the event by one week.
decide.general: I decided to walk instead of waiting for the bus.

knowledge.natural: His knowledge of the area saved the team time.
knowledge.positive: Knowledge shared with others multiplies in value.
knowledge.leadership: A leader builds the team's knowledge instead of guarding his own.
knowledge.factual: Knowledge of first aid is compulsory for all instructors.
knowledge.general: Her knowledge of films is amazing.

group.natural: He joined the group and listened before speaking.
group.positive: A group achieves more when every voice is heard.
group.leadership: The leader divided the group into pairs for the search.
group.factual: The group had twelve members and one guide.
group.general: Our study group meets every Thursday.

confidence.natural: Her confidence grew with every successful attempt.
confidence.positive: Confidence built on practice never feels false.
confidence.leadership: A leader builds confidence in others by trusting them with real tasks.
confidence.factual: The candidate answered with confidence and clear reasoning.
confidence.general: He spoke with confidence at the meeting.

value.simple: worth, or to think highly of something
value.natural: He valued the time his parents gave him.
value.positive: Values guide a person when rules are not watching.
value.leadership: A leader values honest feedback more than flattery.
value.factual: The value of the old coin had risen sharply.
value.general: This watch is good value for the price.

improve.natural: He improved a little every day without noticing it.
improve.positive: Anyone can improve with honest practice and patience.
improve.leadership: The leader improved the routine after hearing the team's complaints.
improve.factual: The unit's timing improved by forty seconds in a month.
improve.general: My handwriting improved after I slowed down.

humble.natural: He stayed humble even after the award.
humble.positive: A humble person learns faster than a proud one.
humble.leadership: A leader stays humble enough to say he was wrong.
humble.factual: The general was known for his humble lifestyle.
humble.general: The hut was small and humble but very clean.

zeal.natural: He attacked the task with zeal from the first minute.
zeal.positive: Zeal turns ordinary work into something people notice.
zeal.leadership: The leader's zeal lifted the whole team on the hardest day.
zeal.factual: The volunteers worked with zeal throughout the camp.
zeal.general: She cleaned the kitchen with unexpected zeal.

sympathy.natural: He offered sympathy before offering advice.
sympathy.positive: Sympathy with action becomes real help.
sympathy.leadership: A leader shows sympathy without lowering the standard.
sympathy.factual: The letter expressed sympathy for the families of the injured.
sympathy.general: You have my sympathy after such a long week.

virtue.natural: He trusted her virtue more than her words.
virtue.positive: Patience is a virtue that wins long battles.
virtue.leadership: A leader's first virtue is fairness under pressure.
virtue.factual: Honesty is listed among the core virtues in every culture.
virtue.general: There is some virtue in waiting a day before replying.

hesitate.simple: to wait because you are unsure
hesitate.natural: He hesitated for a second, then stepped forward.
hesitate.positive: A short hesitation can prevent a long mistake.
hesitate.leadership: A leader acts when the moment arrives but does not act blindly.
hesitate.factual: The driver hesitated at the crossing and avoided the accident.
hesitate.general: Do not hesitate to call if you need help.

waste.simple: to use badly or throw away
waste.natural: He hated to waste a single moment of the day.
waste.positive: Avoiding waste is a habit that builds discipline.
waste.leadership: The leader stopped the waste of fuel by planning the route.
waste.factual: The unit recycled water to avoid waste during the camp.
waste.general: Do not waste the food left on your plate.

fortune.simple: luck, or a large amount of money
fortune.natural: He counted his good fortune and thanked his teachers.
fortune.positive: Fortune favours the person who is ready for it.
fortune.leadership: A leader does not depend on fortune, but on preparation.
fortune.factual: The family made a fortune in the textile trade.
fortune.general: We had the good fortune to find the shop open.

demand.simple: to ask firmly, or a strong request
demand.natural: He demanded a clear answer from the seniors.
demand.positive: A fair demand made calmly is easier to meet.
demand.leadership: A leader demands effort, not perfection.
demand.factual: The union demanded a review of the working hours.
demand.general: This job demands a lot of patience.

neglect.simple: to fail to care for something
neglect.natural: He noticed the machine was neglected and oiled it.
neglect.positive: Small attention now prevents great neglect later.
neglect.leadership: A leader never neglects the quiet member of the team.
neglect.factual: The report blamed the delay on years of neglect.
neglect.general: Do not neglect your health for work.

love.natural: He loved the sea from the first time he saw it.
love.positive: Love shown through small actions outlasts words.
love.leadership: A leader shows love for the team through fairness and care.
love.factual: He loved teaching and taught for forty years.
love.general: I love the smell of rain on dry earth.

purpose.natural: He asked the purpose before starting the task.
purpose.positive: A clear purpose makes hard work feel light.
purpose.leadership: A leader gives the team a purpose, not just orders.
purpose.factual: The purpose of the drill was to test reaction time.
purpose.general: The purpose of this meeting is to plan the trip.

appreciate.simple: to recognise the value of something
appreciate.natural: He appreciated the help he received at the start.
appreciate.positive: People appreciate sincere thanks more than gifts.
appreciate.leadership: A leader appreciates effort in public and corrects in private.
appreciate.factual: The report appreciated the team's speed in the rescue.
appreciate.general: I appreciate you waiting for me.

limit.simple: the point beyond which something stops
limit.natural: He knew his limit and rested before it.
limit.positive: Knowing your limit is strength, not weakness.
limit.leadership: A leader respects the team's limits and plans around them.
limit.factual: The speed limit on the highway is eighty kilometres an hour.
limit.general: There is a limit to how many calls I can take.

vice.simple: a bad habit or moral fault
vice.natural: He corrected the vice before it became a habit.
vice.positive: Every vice can be replaced with a better routine.
vice.leadership: A leader checks his own vices before pointing at others.
vice.factual: Gambling is treated as a vice in most traditions.
vice.general: Sleeping late has become a vice for me.

discover.simple: to find something for the first time
discover.natural: He discovered the leak before it damaged the store.
discover.positive: Every mistake helps you discover a better method.
discover.leadership: A leader discovers the real cause before blaming anyone.
discover.factual: The engineer discovered the fault during the routine check.
discover.general: I discovered a new tea shop near the office.

remove.natural: He removed the obstacle and carried on.
remove.positive: Removing excuses is the fastest way to improve.
remove.leadership: The leader removed the team's biggest difficulty first.
remove.factual: The debris was removed from the road within an hour.
remove.general: Please remove your shoes at the door.

opportunity.natural: He took the opportunity before it passed.
opportunity.positive: An opportunity shared with others often grows bigger.
opportunity.leadership: A leader gives the opportunity to the person who needs it most.
opportunity.factual: The scholarship offers an opportunity to study abroad.
opportunity.general: The holiday is a good opportunity to meet family.

empty.natural: He found the room empty and waited outside.
empty.positive: An empty page is a fresh start, not a failure.
empty.leadership: A leader notices the empty seat and asks why it is empty.
empty.factual: The tank was empty after the long journey.
empty.general: The market was empty in the afternoon heat.

favour.simple: an act of kindness, or to prefer
favour.natural: He did the favour without expecting anything back.
favour.positive: A favour given freely returns in unexpected ways.
favour.leadership: A leader never shows favour to one person over another.
favour.factual: The rules do not allow favour to any candidate.
favour.general: Can you do me a favour and hold this bag?

zenith.natural: He reached his zenith after years of steady work.
zenith.positive: The zenith is reached by many small steps, not one leap.
zenith.leadership: A leader plans for the day after the team's zenith.
zenith.factual: The sun is at its zenith at noon.
zenith.general: Their friendship was at its zenith that summer.

judge.simple: to form an opinion, or the person who decides in court
judge.natural: He judged the situation quickly and acted.
judge.positive: Judge yourself by effort and others by intention.
judge.leadership: A leader judges people on results and behaviour, not talk.
judge.factual: The judge heard both sides before giving the order.
judge.general: Do not judge the film before watching it.

valour.natural: He acted with valour when others stepped back.
valour.positive: Valour is courage used for others, not for show.
valour.leadership: A leader's valour is measured by what he does for his team.
valour.factual: The officer was decorated for valour during the operation.
valour.general: The story of his valour is still told in the village.

finish.natural: He finished the work before the deadline.
finish.positive: Finish one task fully before starting the next.
finish.leadership: A leader stays until the last person has finished.
finish.factual: The repairs were finished two days early.
finish.general: Finish your food before the bus comes.

revenge.simple: harm done to someone who hurt you
revenge.natural: He felt the urge for revenge and let it pass.
revenge.positive: Replacing revenge with calm solves the problem faster.
revenge.leadership: A leader refuses revenge and restores fairness instead.
revenge.factual: The dispute ended after mediation instead of revenge.
revenge.general: He bought a new cycle out of revenge.

behave.simple: to act in a certain way
behave.natural: He behaved calmly even when provoked.
behave.positive: Behaving well when nobody is watching is real character.
behave.leadership: A leader behaves the way he expects the team to behave.
behave.factual: The children behaved well throughout the function.
behave.general: Please behave properly in the temple.

worry.natural: He worried about the result until he made a plan.
worry.positive: Worry used as a warning is useful; worry used as a habit is not.
worry.leadership: A leader carries worry quietly so the team stays calm.
worry.factual: The delay worried the passengers at the station.
worry.general: Do not worry about the rain; we have time.

ambition.simple: a strong wish to achieve something
ambition.natural: His ambition kept him studying after work.
ambition.positive: Ambition guided by values builds something lasting.
ambition.leadership: A leader's ambition includes the growth of others.
ambition.factual: Her ambition is to join the Air Force as an engineer.
ambition.general: His ambition is to own a small bakery.

timid.natural: The timid boy answered softly but correctly.
timid.positive: A timid person can become bold through small wins.
timid.leadership: A leader gives the timid member an easy first task.
timid.factual: The timid puppy hid under the chair all evening.
timid.general: She was too timid to ask for a second helping.

failure.natural: He treated the failure as information, not identity.
failure.positive: Failure shows what to change, not what to give up.
failure.leadership: A leader takes the blame for failure and gives the credit away.
failure.factual: The first attempt ended in failure; the second succeeded.
failure.general: The power failure lasted only ten minutes.

apply.simple: to put something to use, or to ask formally
apply.natural: He applied the lesson the next time the situation came.
apply.positive: Knowledge becomes strength only when you apply it.
apply.leadership: A leader applies the rule to himself before anyone else.
apply.factual: The students applied for the scholarship before the deadline.
apply.general: Apply a little oil if the door sticks.

destroy.simple: to damage so badly that nothing remains
destroy.natural: He refused to destroy what could still be repaired.
destroy.positive: Destroying a bad habit is easier than controlling it.
destroy.leadership: A leader destroys rumours before they spread.
destroy.factual: The storm destroyed three houses near the river.
destroy.general: That mistake destroyed his confidence for a while.

honour.simple: respect, or a mark of respect
honour.natural: He felt honoured to carry the flag.
honour.positive: Honour is kept by small honest acts, not by titles.
honour.leadership: A leader protects the honour of his team before his own.
honour.factual: The officer was honoured for saving two lives.
honour.general: It is an honour to meet you.

transfer.simple: to move from one place to another
transfer.natural: He accepted the transfer and settled in quickly.
transfer.positive: A transfer brings new lessons along with new duties.
transfer.leadership: A leader explains the reason for a transfer honestly.
transfer.factual: The officer was transferred to the mountain post in June.
transfer.general: I need to transfer the money by evening.

ugly.natural: The building looked ugly but kept out the cold.
ugly.positive: Ugly situations handled with grace build character.
ugly.leadership: A leader addresses the ugly facts instead of hiding them.
ugly.factual: The ugly stain on the wall came from old damp.
ugly.general: He was in an ugly mood all morning.

optimist.natural: The optimist in him kept looking for another way.
optimist.positive: An optimist works harder because he believes it matters.
optimist.leadership: A leader values optimists, but checks their plans.
optimist.factual: The survey found optimists sleep better than pessimists.
optimist.general: My uncle is a true optimist about the weather.

follow.natural: He followed the plan exactly until it stopped working.
follow.positive: Good followers make good leaders later.
follow.leadership: A leader follows the rules he asks others to follow.
follow.factual: The truck followed the ridge road for four hours.
follow.general: Follow the lane until you reach the school.

danger.natural: He sensed the danger and stopped the team.
danger.positive: Danger faced with preparation becomes a challenge.
danger.leadership: A leader warns the team and never hides the danger.
danger.factual: The bridge was marked as a danger to traffic.
danger.general: There is danger of slipping on the wet floor.

secure.natural: He secured the door before leaving.
secure.positive: Small precautions keep a home secure.
secure.leadership: The leader secured the group's position before sending a radio message.
secure.factual: The perimeter was secured by midnight.

victory.simple: winning or success in a contest
victory.natural: He celebrated the victory quietly with the team.
victory.positive: A victory shared is remembered longer than one claimed alone.
victory.leadership: A leader credits the victory to the whole team.
victory.factual: The victory came after two days of play.
victory.general: Winning the match was a victory for the whole school.

language.simple: the words people use to communicate
language.natural: He learned the local language to talk with the villagers.
language.positive: Language builds bridges where differences divide.
language.leadership: A leader speaks in a language the whole team understands.

stable.natural: He kept the boat stable in the crossing.
stable.positive: A stable mind handles sudden change well.
stable.leadership: A leader provides stability during confusing times.
stable.factual: The patient's condition was stable by morning.
stable.general: We need a stable internet connection.

young.natural: The young recruit surprised everyone with his endurance.
young.positive: Young energy with good guidance achieves amazing results.
young.leadership: A leader invests time in young people.
young.factual: The young officer was the youngest in his batch.
young.general: The young trees need water every day.

command.simple: to order, or the power to order
command.natural: He gave the command clearly and repeated the key part.
command.positive: Command earned by respect works better than command by fear.
command.leadership: A leader commands the situation without raising his voice.
command.factual: The command was issued from the control room.
command.general: He has command over three languages.

friend.simple: a person you like and trust
friend.natural: He called his friend before the long journey.
friend.positive: A true friend tells you what you need to hear.
friend.leadership: A leader is approachable, not just friendly.
friend.factual: The two friends joined the academy together.

criticise.natural: He criticised the plan, not the person.
criticise.positive: Honest criticism improves the work if it is specific.
criticise.leadership: A leader criticises in private and praises in public.
criticise.factual: The report criticised the delay in repairs.
criticise.general: Do not criticise the food before tasting it.

mature.simple: able to act sensibly like an adult
mature.natural: He was mature enough to accept the decision.
mature.positive: Maturity is choosing what is right over what is easy.
mature.leadership: A leader stays mature when others lose their temper.
mature.factual: The fruit becomes mature by the end of summer.
mature.general: She is very mature for her age.

pressure.natural: He kept working well under pressure.
pressure.leadership: A leader shields the team from needless pressure.
pressure.factual: The water pressure dropped after the repair.
pressure.general: There is too much pressure to finish today.

uniform.simple: the same clothing worn by a group
uniform.natural: He kept his uniform neat even after the exercise.
uniform.positive: A uniform reminds you that the group matters before self.
uniform.leadership: A leader wears the uniform with the same discipline as the newest cadet.
uniform.factual: The uniform was issued on the first day of the course.
uniform.general: She wore her school uniform with pride.

invite.natural: He invited the whole street to the wedding.
invite.positive: Inviting others in turns a house into a home.
invite.leadership: A leader invites ideas from the quietest member.
invite.factual: The chief guest invited questions from the audience.
invite.general: Let us invite them for tea.

develop.natural: He developed a habit of reading every night.
develop.positive: Skills develop quietly over months of practice.
develop.leadership: The leader develops the team's strengths and covers its gaps.
develop.factual: The area developed quickly after the new road arrived.

accident.natural: He reached the accident site before the police.
accident.positive: An accident prevented by care is the best kind.
accident.leadership: The leader kept order at the accident until help came.
accident.factual: The accident was caused by a burst tyre.
accident.general: I met your brother by accident at the market.

nature.simple: the natural world or someone's character
nature.natural: He spent the evening quietly with nature.
nature.leadership: A leader understands the nature of the problem before acting.
nature.factual: Nature conservation protects both forests and wildlife.
nature.general: It is in his nature to help.
